acceptance: docs/agent/review-protocol.md, or a page it links, states the three behaviours and the exact reply format for a dispute.
The text is checked against the reviewer's current behaviour in the Theseus repository before it is written, and names the Theseus version it was checked against.
If the instruction-file byte budget has no room, the text goes in a linked reference page, not in the six budgeted instruction files.
context: Correction to the description, checked against Theseus 0.2.12: a top-level pull request comment `Dispute: D<n> - <reason>` does clear a finding when its author is listed in consumer.attesters, the comment is unedited, posted after the review that listed the finding, and the finding is still open. A thread reply works only while the thread is unresolved. The recovery page documents both.
description: Three behaviours of the hosted reviewer cost several wasted review rounds on 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12 and are written down nowhere under docs/ on develop. (1) Commenting /review on a head that has not changed only reposts the previous verdict; it does not re-evaluate. (2) A finding carried forward from an earlier head clears only when the author replies 'Dispute: D<n> - <reason>' on the finding's thread while that thread is still unresolved, and then comments /review. Resolving the thread first, or disputing in a top-level comment, leaves the finding in force. (3) A review that reports 'reviewer process is blocked' does not recover by itself; a /review comment restarts it. Agents currently rediscover these by trial, and each wrong attempt spends a review run. Related open item oracle-review-comment-skipped-on-backoff-after-dispute-20261101 covers one failure after a dispute, not the procedure.
